summary.headline: Vaibhav Global Q2 FY27 revenue rose 7% to INR 938.4 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 8.1% and FY27 growth guidance was cut to 7-9%.
summary.overview: Q2 was a transition quarter as Vaibhav moved all six retail websites to Shopify Enterprise and consolidated four UK warehouses and two studios into one site. Management attributed about $2.8 million (roughly 2.8 percentage points) of revenue growth loss to the platform migration. Gross margin expanded about 197 bps to 65.5%, but EBITDA margin fell 193 bps to 8.1% on deleverage in the US and UK. FY27 revenue growth guidance was cut to 7-9% from 9-11%, and FY27 margin is now expected broadly flat versus FY26 instead of 50-100 bps expansion.

financial_highlights.change: +5.6% YoY in INR, -4.2% in constant currency

segments.name: US
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 500 crore in Q2, +4.3% in INR and -4.1% in constant currency; units +4.8% while ASP fell 8.4%. EBITDA margin 5.7% in Q2 on sales deleverage from CTV, OTT and app advertising; H1 US EBITDA INR 86.6 crore, +24.9%, margin 8.4% (+102 bps).

segments.name: UK
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 257.2 crore, +2.3% in INR and -7% in constant currency, the weakest region. Drivers were the platform migration, product unavailability during warehouse consolidation (INR 36 crore capex) and weak consumer sentiment.

segments.name: Europe ex-UK
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 110 crore, +18.3% in INR and +8% in constant currency, with units +11.5%. Germany (Shopify Germany) grew 5.8% and Mindful Source grew 12.7%. Europe loss narrowed to INR 0.7 crore in H1 from INR 6.6 crore a year earlier.

segments.name: B2B
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 70.9 crore in Q2, +32% YoY, described as another strong quarter.

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: In-house brands were 57% of B2C revenue. Lab-grown diamonds rose to about 12% of total retail revenue from about 10% a year earlier. Lifestyle products were about 40% of B2C revenue and Budget Pay about 35% of retail revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance cut to 7-9% from 9-11%, citing the Shopify migration impact, UK consolidation, weaker UK consumer and US midterm elections.
FY27 EBITDA margin now expected broadly in line with FY26, versus earlier guidance of 50-100 bps expansion.
Management remains confident of returning to 9-11% revenue growth in FY28, led by digital.
Digital share of B2C revenue targeted at 50% by Q4 FY27; medium-term target of 50% lifestyle share.
Medium-term revenue target of INR 5,500 crore by FY30 excludes any new country launch such as India; some small digital e-commerce acquisition is contemplated.
Sustainable effective tax rate guided at 18-40% in the medium term, with German losses still to be absorbed beyond FY28.
Second interim dividend of INR 15 per share declared (figure stated inconsistently in transcript); first interim dividend was also declared in Q1 FY27.
capex_capacity: UK warehouse consolidation from four warehouses and two studios into one site; about INR 36 crore invested, with benefits expected in coming years from order clubbing and efficiency.
Q2 investment also covered tech improvements and the Shopify migration; total Q2 capex cited as INR 63 crore.
Inventory up about INR 100 crore year on year ahead of festive season; inventory days expected to normalise to 200-220 by Q3-Q4.
Management stated capital allocation priority: digital growth, proprietary brands, lab-grown diamonds, Germany profitability and UK operating improvement.
demand_pricing: Retail volumes grew about 2% in Q2, driven by lower price point items as consumers traded down; US ASP fell 8.4%.

Management said the UK consumer environment weakened: UK inflation was 3.5% in September, UK food retail sales were flat, and UK consumer confidence had its sharpest monthly fall since 2020 in October.
Management said gross margin expansion reflects vertical integration, in-house brands and lab-grown diamonds, and that metal price movements have not had a material impact on margins.
Shipping costs rose with volume growth, and the EBITDA bridge included about 100 bps from Shopify and UK warehouse disruption and about 30 bps from one-time items in the prior year.
Customer base: about 687,000 unique customers and 360,000 new customers acquired over the trailing period, 38% retention, and about 23 pieces bought per customer per year (as stated).

qa_highlights.question: Shareholder question on buybacks, given the stock's fall and continued dividends.
qa_highlights.answer: Board discussed it and chose to keep paying dividends while building cash for acquisitions or strategic moves. Management said any surplus cash after that would be deployed for buyback.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify the Shopify migration revenue loss and the reason for the INR 63 crore capex.
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue impact was about $2.8 million, or about 2.8 percentage points of growth. The capex was mainly INR 36 crore for UK warehouse consolidation plus tech and Shopify migration spend.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital rise, and when will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory was up about INR 100 crore year on year for festive readiness and global uncertainty. Management expects it to moderate in Q3 and Q4 to 200-220 inventory days.

qa_highlights.question: Strategy on gold and metal prices, and whether margins can be held.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margin moved from about 62% to 64-65% despite higher metal prices. It will respond to market prices in real time and keep the growth trajectory in line with guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why is US market share only about 2%, and what is the customer acquisition target?
qa_highlights.answer: The US is the most competitive market. Target customer payback is within six months, with a long-term aim of about three months. The core customer is white females aged 40+.

qa_highlights.question: What is the lab-grown diamond opportunity and does it displace natural stones?
qa_highlights.answer: LGD is about 12% of Q2 revenue. Management said LGD largely displaced natural diamonds, and that natural demand is starting to recover; the company tests categories on contribution per minute and screen space.

risks_watch: Digital growth must return to around 20% for 9-11% group growth; digital declined 4.2% in constant currency in Q2, and the TV base is attriting.
UK remains weak (-7% constant currency) and may keep dragging group growth until the warehouse consolidation and platform stabilise.
Margin: FY27 EBITDA margin is now guided flat, and Q2 EBITDA margin fell to 8.1%. Watch US customer acquisition costs against the six-month payback target.
Inventory-led working capital build (about INR 100 crore) and net cash decline from INR 279 crore to INR 186 crore.
Shareholder pressure on capital returns: a buyback was requested and rejected for now, with dividends kept.
US midterm election impact on TV viewership and the wider macro in the UK and Germany.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term digital platform and FY28 recovery, but openly cautious and defensive on the near-term guidance cut, the UK and the Shopify transition costs. Management was evasive on buyback and specific customer retention data, offering to share later.
key_quotes: Q2 was a quarter of transition and an important one.
We now expect revenue growth of 7 to 9% in FY27 compared with the earlier guidance of 9 to 11%.
We believe this is the right call and it does not change our medium-term view.
We want to be digital first company not a legacy TV company going forward.

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guidance cut to 7-9% (midpoint 8%) from 9-11%, with EBITDA margin now flat vs FY26; Q2 revenue +7% YoY, but support is mostly a Shopify migration recovery, digital share target of 50% by Q4 FY27 and a FY28 return to 9-11%, with no specific capacity or order book quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA margin now guided broadly flat vs FY26, down from 50-100 bps expansion; Q2 EBITDA margin fell 193 bps to 8.1% on US and UK deleverage and about 100 bps of Shopify/UK warehouse disruption.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant, line or store capacity is discussed; the only footprint change is consolidating four UK warehouses and two studios into one site (about INR 36 crore), which reduces capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Retail volumes grew about 2% in Q2 and US units rose 4.8%, but UK is -7% in constant currency and digital fell 4.2% in constant currency, so growth depends on a Shopify and UK recovery.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Q2 capex was INR 63 crore and utilisation was not given, so no capex plan is stated; a buyback or acquisition-led deployment of cash is more likely than a plant, and management is building cash for acquisitions.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth guidance was cut to 7-9% from 9-11% and margin guidance to flat, so the call points to lower, not higher, guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue grew 9.7% but Q2 was only 7% with -1% constant currency; the guide already assumes a recovery in H2, and UK is -7% in constant currency with consumer confidence at its sharpest monthly fall since 2020.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Lab-grown diamonds are about 12% of retail revenue (up from 10%), and digital share is targeted at 50% of B2C by Q4 FY27, but no specific new product or brand launch date was given.

rows.label: Digital and UK recovery back to 9-11% growth in FY28
rows.why: Management is confident of 9-11% growth in FY28, but digital must return to about 20% growth from -4.2% constant currency in Q2 and UK is -7% constant currency.

rows.label: Buyback or acquisition deployment of surplus cash
rows.why: Net cash fell to INR 186 crore from INR 279 crore; the board kept dividends and is building cash for acquisitions, with buyback only if surplus remains.

rows.label: Inventory days normalise to 200-220
rows.why: Inventory was up about INR 100 crore YoY for festive readiness, and management guided inventory days back to 200-220 by Q3-Q4.

tone.note: Management was confident on the digital platform and the FY28 return to 9-11% growth, but cautious and defensive on the cut to FY27 guidance, UK weakness and Shopify transition costs; analysts pressed on buybacks, capital allocation and customer retention, which management was evasive about.

oneOffs.what: Shopify platform migration and UK warehouse consolidation cost about $2.8 million (about 2.8 percentage points) of Q2 revenue growth
About 30 bps of the EBITDA margin bridge came from one-time items in the prior year, depressing Q2 margin growth (profit, not revenue)
